episode_title: Ben Shapiro reassesses the president he campaigned for | Newsmakers
script_en: Ben Shapiro reassesses the president he campaigned for | Newsmakers.
Conservative host Ben Shapiro says he is holding to his conservative values in the unstable era of President Trump.
The host of The Ben Shapiro Show voted against Trump in 2016 but also campaigned for him in 2024.
He’s disappointed in the president’s tariffs, alleged corruption and the execution of the Iran war.
“I regret the way the president has performed,” Shapiro tells host Steve Inskeep in this episode of Newsmakers .

I don't have a time machine.” Shapiro says Trump’s aggressive immigration enforcement and the general “whiff of corruption” that surrounds the White House — specifically the Trump family’s crypto company World Liberty Financial — all contributed to the Republican Party’s midterm losses in Congress, governor's mansions and state legislatures.
He believes that Republicans have an “uphill road in 2028” and that Vice President Vance isn’t the ideal Republican presidential candidate.
He argues that Vance would shrink Trump’s winning 2024 voting bloc of Hispanics, the working class, women and college-educated individuals.
Shapiro points to Secretary of State Marco Rubio as a potential 2028 Republican candidate with broader appeal and a larger coalition.
But he says many within the current White House will likely be damaged by association.
Shapiro also unpacks his new movie, Confession — featuring Rob Lowe and James Franco — and the recent decline in his show’s YouTube subscriptions.
